Summaries

five sample summaries

[1] : Steve Jobs gave a speech at Stanford University. In his speech, he talked about three important stories from his life.First, he talked about connecting the dots. He dropped out of college, but he took a calligraphy class because he was interested in it. At that time, he did not know that it would be useful. Later, what he learned helped him create beautiful fonts for the Macintosh. He said that we cannot connect the dots looking forward. We can only connect them looking backwards. He encouraged people to trust that their experiences will be useful in the future.Second, he talked about love and loss. He was fired from Apple when he was about 30, but he did not give up. He started NeXT and Pixar and continued doing what he loved.Finally, he talked about death. He said that remembering death helped him make important choices and live without regrets. He encouraged people to follow their hearts and live their own lives.                                                                                                                                                                                   
[2] He gave a speech to the audience at Stanford Uni. in 2005. He talked about three topics, connecting the dots, love and loss and death. The first one he talks about is about connecting the dots. He took the calligraphy class after he dropped out and he thought this was fascinating. Ten years later, when he tried making the computer, he used the techniques in the computer. So everyone doesn't know the future but do something, which the dots will somehow connect. The second one is about love and loss. He ran his own business but he was fired from that. When he didn't work for the company, he did another job ( it is now known as the best animation company in the world.) And he returned back. The third one is about death. He was diagnosed with cancer by a doctor. He had little life to be left. However, he looked in the mirror and asked himself. If today is the last day, what will I do and what am I about to do? Do the things as soon as possible, not do another day.                                                                                                                                        
[3] The first story is about connecting the dots. He stated, "And much of what I stumbled into by following my curiosity and intuition turned out to be priceless later on." Even though none of this had even a hope of any practical application in his life, he later proved how it mattered with the creation of the Mac. He says that you can only connect them looking backwards. Believing that the dots will connect down the road will give you the confidence to follow your heart even when it leads you off the well-worn path, and that will make all the difference. The second story is about love and loss. Life sometimes hits you hard, but you must never lose hope and must find what you love. Doing what you love is the only way to be truly satisfied. The third story is about death. Remembering that you are going to die is the most important tool to help you make big choices in life. While going through life, there are many hardships and moments when we push ourselves too hard trying to meet expectations, but facing the reality of death helps us realize what truly matters. Death is the ultimate change maker.
[4] Steve Jobs gave a speech at Stanford University in 2005. He talked about three important stories from his life and shared lessons with the graduates. The first story was about connecting the dots. Jobs dropped out of college after six months because he did not know why calligraphy would be useful, but later the knowledge helped him create beautiful fonts and designs for apple products. His experience taught him that we cannot always understand how different experiences will connect in the future. The second story was about love and loss. Jobs was fired from Apple, the company he helped create. Although it was very painful, he later realized that being fired gave him the chance to start new projects. Eventually, he returned to Apple. The third story was about death. After being diagnosed with cancer, Jobs realized that life is short. He encouraged people to follow their own hearts instead of living according to other people`s expectations. He ended his speech with the message, Stay hungry, stay foolish.                                                                                             
[5] Jobs tells three stories and the first is "connecting dots”. When he was a university student he dropped out. Because he thinks that the learning does not help to find what he really want to do in his life and have no idea how college is going to help me figure it out. He couldn’t find the value in it and he wants his parents to use thor money for their entire life. His second story is love and loss. He was lucky because he could find what he loved. He created pixer and so on. He says that the important thing is true for work as it is for lovers. He also thinks thatOnly great work leads you that what I want to do. His thers story is about death. He always thinks that if today is the last day of life, what I do today is the most important thing for me. He says that concerning death is a good way to make a big detision.and finally he concludes “stay hungry stay foolishi”, and it means that I am not satisfied with the real situation and believe myself.

[3] What left the strongest impression on me was his words that death is life’s change agent. As long as we are born as living beings, death treats everyone equally, whether you are a person of great character or wealthy. Except for those who are ill, probably no one goes through each day consciously realizing that they could die at any moment, and I am one of them. Asking yourself in front of the mirror every day what you want to do with your life will help you realize the true importance of living your own life.I was able to realize that thinking about death is not a negative thing, but rather a necessary one.                        
[4] I was impressed by Steve Jobs’ message that we should follow our own hearts. I think this is important because we sometimes worry too much about what other people think. We may choose a school or a job because other people think it is a good choice. However, it may not be what we really want. Jobs also said that we cannot understand how our experiences are connected until we look back. I agree with this idea because even small experiences can become useful in the future. His story made me think that we should not be afraid of making mistakes or changing our plans. I want to try things that interest me and learn from my experiences.
[5] Jobs' speech taught me that failure is never a waste of time. I experienced this when I performed baton twirling in high school. During the Tokyo regional competition, our team made mistakes and performed poorly, which was very disappointing. However, we did not give up. We practiced harder, corrected our mistakes, and successfully performed at the Kanto competition. Like Jobs said, connecting the dots only happens when looking back. That failure helped us grow and succeed in the end. His speech reminded me to trust my journey, learn from my mistakes, and always keep trying without fear of failure.
